unit.title: Perpetual Review
unit.summary: Mixed retrieval across the whole course: four review templates for daily, weekly and term-based practice.

lessons.title: Daily Bite
lessons.objective: Review one card from your due concepts.

payload.prompt: After the serve and return bounce, who may volley?

explanation.correct: Once both the serve and return have bounced, either team may volley freely.
explanation.incorrect: After two bounces, everyone is free to volley anywhere outside the kitchen.
explanation.sayThisLine: Two bounces, then everyone can volley.

payload.template: A dink is a {{shot-type}} shot that lands in the {{location}}.

explanation.correct: Dinks are soft shots that land in the kitchen, a key strategy in pickleball.
explanation.incorrect: Dinking is the soft game; the ball lands in the opponent's kitchen zone.
explanation.sayThisLine: Soft shot, opponent's kitchen. That's a dink.

pairs.definition: Hitting the ball before it bounces while standing in the non-volley zone.
A soft defensive shot that neutralizes pace and lands in the kitchen.

explanation.summary: Volley in kitchen = fault. Reset = soft defensive shot.
explanation.sayThisLine: Kitchen volleys are faults; resets save you from getting attacked.

options.text: When it bounces on your side
When it's high enough to hit down at

explanation.correct: Attackable means the ball is high enough (above net height) to hit aggressively downward.
explanation.incorrect: You attack when the ball pops up high enough to hit down. That's your chance.
explanation.sayThisLine: High ball = attackable. Time to speed up.

lessons.title: Weekly Mix
lessons.objective: Three-round session sampled across concepts you find harder.

payload.prompt: What's a foot fault on the serve?

options.text: Standing on or past the baseline before hitting

explanation.correct: Foot fault is when you step on or over the baseline before or while serving.
explanation.incorrect: Stay behind the baseline when you serve; stepping over is a fault.
explanation.sayThisLine: Foot fault: over the baseline on the serve.

payload.prompt: A toe touching the kitchen line while volleying is a fault.

scene.alt: Foot position at kitchen line during volley.

explanation.correct: For volleys, the kitchen line counts as being in the kitchen. Toes on the line = fault.
explanation.incorrect: The line is kitchen; even touching it while volleying is a fault.
explanation.sayThisLine: Kitchen line is part of the kitchen for the volley rule.

payload.prompt: Your team just returned serve. What's the smart third shot?

situation.narrative: You're the serving team recovering from the return.

options.label: Soft drop into their kitchen
options.consequence: Correct. This buys time to advance to the net.

options.label: Hard drive at them
options.consequence: Could work but you're starting behind; better to be patient.
considerations: You need time to reach net

payload.expertNote: Third-shot drop philosophy: patience buys time to control the net.

payload.title: Rating talk snippet
payload.setting: Your person mentions a tournament player.

exchanges.theirMessage: That guy said he's a 3.0 but played like a 4.0 today.

replies.text: Sounds like sandbagging? Did he actually play that well?
replies.theirResponse: Yeah, way better than his rating. Weird.
replies.coachNote: You named it and asked for detail. Good.

replies.theirResponse: Maybe, but he played that way the whole time.
replies.coachNote: Could happen, but sandbag is more likely here.
Open play has no refs. Don't escalate casually.

payload.closingNote: Sandbagging is playing above your stated rating. Rec tournaments care; open play, less so.

lessons.title: Kitchen and Score Boss
lessons.objective: Mastery check: the two most-misunderstood areas (kitchen momentum and scoring logic).

payload.prompt: Watch and judge: is this a kitchen violation?

explanation.correct: Momentum carries the player into the kitchen after volleying outside it. That's a fault.
explanation.incorrect: A volley outside the kitchen is fine, but if your momentum carries you in, it's a fault.

payload.prompt: At 0-0-2, the first serving team has already had their second server turn. True?

explanation.correct: 0-0-2 means the first server just served and missed; it's only the first server's turn.
explanation.incorrect: The 2 in 0-0-2 means only one server has played. This is the exception for the first serving team.
explanation.sayThisLine: 0-0-2: first server just faulted. Only one server gets to serve at the start.

payload.prompt: The score is 6-4-1. Where does server 1 stand?

situation.narrative: Serving side's score is 6. You need to know the service side.

options.label: Right service box
options.consequence: Correct. 6 is even, so right side. Even right, odd left.

options.label: Left service box
options.consequence: No. Even scores serve from the right. Odd from left.

payload.expertNote: Even right, odd left. Memorize this for score calls.

payload.prompt: You volley 2 feet outside the kitchen line and the ball lands in. Legal?

explanation.correct: Volleying outside the kitchen is always legal, even if the ball lands in the kitchen.
explanation.incorrect: As long as you volley outside the kitchen, it doesn't matter where the ball goes.
explanation.sayThisLine: Volley outside = legal, no matter where the ball goes.

payload.prompt: On a return of serve, can you volley it if the serve bounced?

options.text: Yes, it bounced so you can volley
No, you must let it bounce
Only if it's a drop serve
Only if you're at the net

explanation.correct: The return must bounce; volleying a return is a fault.
explanation.incorrect: Two-bounce rule: serve bounces, return bounces, then you can volley.
explanation.sayThisLine: Serve bounces, return bounces. Then volley.

lessons.title: Term Blitz
lessons.objective: Playbook term drill: identify and define key vocabulary.

pairs.definition: A jump or stride outside the kitchen to volley near the net post.
A shot that goes around the net post rather than over it.

explanation.summary: Erne = around the post by you. ATP = around the post by the ball.
explanation.sayThisLine: Erne is you going around; ATP is the ball going around.

payload.prompt: Complete these shot and position definitions.
payload.template: An {{shot}} is hit from overhead when the ball is {{height}}. Ready position is {{pos}}.

options: paddle up, knees bent, ready to move
gaps.correct: paddle up, knees bent, ready to move

explanation.correct: Smash = overhead high balls. Ready = athletic stance with paddle up.
explanation.sayThisLine: Paddle up, ready to react. Smash the lobs.

pairs.definition: Both partners start on the same side to keep strengths aligned.
One partner crosses to intercept the opponent's ball meant for the other.

explanation.summary: Stacking = starting position. Poaching = mid-rally interception.
explanation.sayThisLine: Stack before the point; poach during it.

payload.template: A {{term1}} is when a partner runs behind you. A {{term2}} is an MLP {{event}}.

explanation.correct: Bert = partner behind. DreamBreaker = MLP tiebreak at 2-2 to 21 points.
explanation.incorrect: These terms come from the game itself and from pro leagues.
explanation.sayThisLine: Bert is chaos. DreamBreaker is MLP's answer to a tie.
